MIND. [1] [Ant. t.]
Stupid and sleepy ; stupefying meningitis.
Delirium, with pleasant expression. θ Bronchial catarrh.
Pitiful whining before and during attacks. θ Infantile catarrh.
Continual crying and whining of a child for three days, gets only little sleeps of fifteen or thirty minutes. θ Summer complaint.
Bad humor. θ Bronchial catarrh.
Hopelessness, despondency.
Hopeless mood. θ Colic.
Hopeless and despairing when awake. θ Intermittent.
Despondent, hypochondriacal ; inclined to violence.
Melancholic. θ Chronic metritis.
Complains about his numerous symptoms. θ Pneumonia.
Despairs of his recovery. θ Pneumonia.
Anxiety during paroxysm, often lasting two to three hours. θ Pregnancy.
Indescribable anxiety and oppression of chest. θ Cholera.
Anxiety. θ Intermittent.
After attacks, in good humor, playing. θ Catarrhal croup.
Excessively peevish and quarrelsome (a boy æt. 3).
Peevishness. θ Laryngo-tracheitis.
The children get angry, weep and cry. θ Whooping cough.
Worse after getting angry. θ Cough.
Strong emotion followed by amblyopia. θ During pregnancy.
   

SENSORIUM. [2] [Ant. t.]
Pressing pain in forehead with vertigo, stupor and dulness of head, slightly delirious, drowsiness, but cannot sleep. θ Influenza.
Vertigo with flickering before eyes. θ Rheumatism.
Vertigo with dimness of vision and a pressing headache. θ Pneumonia.
Child gets insensible, limbs cold, pulse weak, almost imperceptible ; recovery after brandy and water.
   

INNER HEAD. [3] [Ant. t.]
Cerebral congestion.
Headache, as from a band compressing forehead.
Feels as if brain was pressed together ; stupid and sleepy ; more when resting ; in evenings and at night ; > when moving about, or after washing head.
Heavy pain in forehead like waves increasing and decreasing.
Throbbing in right forehead, < evenings, sitting bent, from warmth and > sitting up and in cold.
Stupefying headache. θ Meningitis.
Headache. θ Variola.
Violent headache during heat. θ Tertian.
Headache also in apyrexia. θ Intermittent.
Inflammation of brain.
Apoplexia nervosa and serosa.
   

OUTER HEAD. [4] [Ant. t.]
Head very hot. θ Rheumatism.
Tinea.
Plica polonica.
Head hot and sweaty. θ Atelectasis pulmonum. θ During efforts at vomiting. θ Pertussis.
   

SIGHT AND EYES. [5] [Ant. t.]
Amblyopia. θ Meningitis.
Oversensitive retina.
Photophobia. θ In scrofulous persons.
Cataract. θ Of cattle.
Eyes turned upward, with difficult breathing. θ Catarrhal croup.
Dim, swimming eyes. θ Diarrhœa.
Eyes prominent, glaring. θ Pneumonia.
Eyes sunken.
Eyes sunken and surrounded by dark circles. θ Cholera.
Edges of lids covered with mucus. θ Pneumonia.
Eyes slightly inflamed, staring, dull, unsteady, half open or one closed. θ Pneumonia.
Eyes somewhat reddened, aching with suppuration of lids. θ Rheumatism.
Gonorrhœal ophthalmia.
Ophthalmia rheumatica or arthritica.
   

SMELL AND NOSE. [7] [Ant. t.]
Uncontrollable epistaxis with spongy gums, as in scurvy.
Nose dry. θ Rheumatism.
Well-marked motion of alæ nasi with a child. θ Pertussis.
Nose pointed.
Nostrils black, smoky, inflated and moving rapidly, like wings. θ Pneumonia.
   

UPPER FACE. [8] [Ant. t.]
Face expresses greatest anxiety. θ Acute œdema of lungs.
Anxious look. θ Bronchial croup.
Despairing anxiety depicted on face. θ Pneumonia.
Suffering face, livid red. θ Pneumonia.
Remarkable distortion of countenance with spasms.
Convulsive twitches in almost every muscle of face. θ With cough.
Tearing pain in whole side of face, even head and neck of that side. θ Rheumatic toothache.
Face very much flushed. θ Catarrhal croup.
Face red, puffed. θ Bronchial croup.
Face red, bloated, anxious. θ Pneumonia.
Pallor. θ Bronchial catarrh.
Pale, sunken face. θ Diarrhœa. θ Cholera.
Face pale, circumscribed redness on cheeks. θ Catarrh.
Face cool, pale earthy, bluish around nose. θ Pneumonia.
Face as pale as a corpse, with bluish spots, distorted and cold. θ Cholera.
Face pale, nose pointed, eyes sunken with blue margins ; lips livid. θ Asphyxia. θ Child after birth.
Cold and livid countenance, bathed in cold sweat.
Pustules on face ; sometimes they leave ugly blue-red scars.
If ulcers last awhile on limbs, ulcers also appear on face. θ Leprosy.
   

LOWER FACE. [9] [Ant. t.]
When gaping he cannot open the mouth fully. θ Intermittent.
Mouth remained open after gaping, he could not shut it for a while. θ Intermittent.
Mouth open, parched, upper lip drawn up. θ Pneumonia.
Eruption around mouth, of rheumatic origin. θ Tertian.
Aphthæ around mouth. θ Influenza.
   

TEETH AND GUMS. [10] [Ant. t.]
Rheumatic toothache of intermitting type.
During dentition catarrhal hyperemia.
   

TASTE, SPEECH, TONGUE. [11] [Ant. t.]
Mouth slightly bitter. θ Pregnancy.
Flat or bitter taste. θ Influenza.
Bitter taste in mouth, especially all night. θ Dyspepsia.
Tongue has a thick white fur. θ Rheumatism.
Thick, white or bilious fur on tongue, with retching of phlegm, nausea and vomiting. θ Influenza.
Tongue, brown, dry. θ Pneumonia.
   

INNER MOUTH. [12] [Ant. t.]
Small, circular patches, like smallpox pustules, in and upon mouth and tongue. θ Diphtheria.
Salivation. θ During pregnancy.
   

PALATE AND THROAT. [13] [Ant. t.]
Much mucus in throat with short breathing.
Throat full of phlegm, with cough.
Dysphagia. θ Meningitis.
   

APPETITE, THIRST. DESIRES, AVERSIONS. [14] [Ant. t.]
Less appetite in apyrexia. θ Tertian intermittent.
Loss of appetite, without much thirst. θ Influenza.
Weariness, with no appetite ; in apyrexia. θ Tertian.
Disgust for food, frequent nausea and relief by vomiting. θ Gastric derangement.
Little thirst, no appetite. θ Rheumatism.
Not much appetite, no thirst. θ Pregnancy.
No appetite, great thirst. θ Rheumatism. θ Pneumonia.
Very little thirst. θ Acute catarrh.
Thirstlessness. θ Diarrhœa. θ Bronchial catarrh.
Great thirst.
Greedy desire for water. θ Summer complaint.
Irresistible thirst for cold water. θ Catarrhal diarrhœa.
Much thirst ; drinks little and often.
Desire for acids, for fruits, or for any cold drink. θ Diarrhœa.
Aversion to milk. θ Diarrhœa.
Aversion and disgust for milk and every other kind of nourishment ; child æt. 3 months. θ Summer complaint.
   

EATING AND DRINKING. [15] [Ant. t.]
Worse after warm drinks, especially milk. θ Whooping cough.
After eating he vomits ingesta, but without relief. θ Pertussis.
Eating sour food or drinking tart wine brings on attack. θ Asthma.
After every drink, nausea and pressure in pit of stomach. θ Pneumonia.
Febrile motion after every meal, with pungent heat in face. θ Pregnancy.
   

HICCOUGH, BELCHING, NAUSEA AND VOMITING. [16] [Ant. t.]
Belching, which relieves. θ During pregnancy.
Foul eructations. θ Pneumonia.
Qualmishness in stomach after dinner.
Nausea causes great anxiety. θ Diarrhœa.
Continuous anxious nausea, straining to vomit, with sweat on forehead. θ Diarrhœa.
Nausea with restlessness and great anxiety. θ Rheumatism.
Nausea with faintness. θ Pregnancy.
Nausea during loose stools.
Long-continued tormenting nausea. θ Yellow fever.
Nausea and incessant vomiting all night.
Nausea, vomiting and want of appetite. θ Intermittent.
Nausea with frequent vomiting of bitter-sour substances. θ Dyspepsia.
Nausea and vomiting with constipation. θ Pneumonia of drunkards. θ Remittent fever.
Copious vomiting. θ Cholera.
Vomits even smallest quantity of drink, with eager desire for water. θ Summer complaint.
Vomits food and drink, even before attack. θ Pertussis.
Violent retching and vomiting food with cough.
Vomits with great effort. θ Diarrhœa.
Vomituritio with diarrhœa, great masses of phlegm brought up. θ Pertussis.
Vomits tenacious mucus. θ Diphtheria.
Vomiting of slime and bile ; of tough, watery mucus, then pasty food, then fluid, mixed with bile ; of bilious masses with great violence ; of bitter, mushy and fluid matter of a bad odor, and acid reaction ; matter tinged with blood ; bloody foaming fluid.
Gastric and bilious vomiting with bitter taste in mouth, vomiting bitter-sour.
Vomiting bloody mucus. θ Pneumonia in children.
Hæmoptysis. θ Delirium tremens.
Vomiting in any position, except lying on right side ; with headache and trembling of hands.
During efforts of vomiting, head hot and sweaty. θ Pertussis.
Vomiting and fainting. θ Meningitis.
Vomiting and diarrhœa in August, with a child, æt. three months.
Vomiting is followed by great languor, drowsiness, loathing, desire for cooling things. θ Diarrhœa.
In morning vomiting and cramps in arms and legs, after diarrhœa all night. θ Cholera.
Retching, then vomiting, followed by great prostration, chilliness and sleepiness.
   

SCROBICULUM AND STOMACH. [17] [Ant. t.]
Tingling and pinching in pit of stomach, with violent, sudden beats of heart. θ Pleurisy.
Pit of stomach sensitive, with meteorism, nausea and vomiting. θ Pneumonia of drunkards.
No pain in pit of stomach or abdomen. θ Cholera.
Sensation of emptiness in stomach. θ Influenza.
   

HYPOCHONDRIA. [18] [Ant. t.]
Great precordial anxiety with vomiting of mucus and bile.
Pressure in hypochondria with distension, most in region of liver. θ Influenza.
Gastric and hypochondriac regions sensitive and distended. θ Pneumonia.
Icterus with pneumonia, especially of right lung.
   

ABDOMEN AND LOINS. [19] [Ant. t.]
Sharp cutting colic before stool. θ Diarrhœa.
Colic, during loose stools.
Most violent pain in abdomen, sacral and coccygeal region and in loins. θ Chronic metritis.
Abdomen tympanitic and very sensitive to pressure. θ Acute catarrh.
Pain in groins and cold creeps before menses. θ Dysmenorrhœa.
   

STOOLS AND RECTUM. [20] [Ant. t.]
Burning at anus, after loose stool.
Tenesmus during and after loose stools.
Violent shifting of flatulence without distension of abdomen, before stool. θ Diarrhœa.
Relief of pains after loose stools.
Frequent, profuse, loose stools.
Mucous diarrhœa with colic and restlessness.
Small, slimy, diarrheic stools. θ Pneumonia.
At times pituitous, not copious diarrhœa. θ Influenza.
Watery, mucous, bloody diarrhœa.
Watery, sometimes slimy and greenish diarrhœa, increased each time after taking breast.
Stools as green as grass, slimy. θ Summer complaint.
Evening, a few watery stools, thirty or forty during night. θ Cholera.
Cholera when vomiting is copious and there is coldness, and threadlike or trembling pulse.
Involuntary stools. θ Meningitis.
Stools : yellowish-brown ; thin, bilious, mucous ; liquid greenish, with heat at anus ; slimy, appearing like yeast and of cadaverous smell ; light brownish-yellow, fecal.
Diarrhœa in pneumonia, smallpox and other eruptive diseases, especially if eruption is suppressed.
Diarrhœa of drunkards.
Stool seldom, somewhat hard, with tenesmus. θ Rheumatism.
Costiveness for several days. θ Acute catarrh.
Constipation with nausea and vomiting. θ Pregnancy.
No stool. θ Pneumonia.
   

URINARY ORGANS. [21] [Ant. t.]
Spasm of bladder, urine scanty and red. θ Pneumonia.
Urine dark brownish-red, turbid, of strong odor ; or becomes cloudy and deposits a violet colored earthy sediment.
Highly reddened urine. θ Pneumonia.
Urine scanty, dark, with a brick-dust sediment. θ Rheumatism.
Violent tension in perineum, especially on walking, with strong inclination to urinate.
Violent and painful urging to urinate, with scanty or bloody discharge. θ Diarrhœa.
Urinary discharge interrupted during whole time ; only in evening, on third day, scanty dark urine. θ Catarrhal croup.
   

MALE SEXUAL ORGANS. [22] [Ant. t.]
Pain in testicles ; after checked gonorrhœa. θ Orchitis.
Warts behind glans penis, with ulcers elsewhere. θ Sycosis.
Pustules on genitals and thighs.
   

FEMALE SEXUAL ORGANS. [23] [Ant. t.]
Sensation as if a heavy weight was tugging at coccyx. θ Chronic metritis.
Severe bearing down in vagina. θ Diarrhœa.
Before menses, pains in groins and cold creepings. θ Dysmenorrhœa.
Violent itching of pudenda. θ Diarrhœa.
   

PREGNANCY. PARTURITION. LACTATION. [24] [Ant. t.]
Gastric derangements ; vomiting of mucus ; belching ; disgust for food ; salivation ; nausea with faintness ; amblyopia after colic or strong emotions.
Puerperal-like convulsions continuing after birth of foetus ; breathing short, difficult ; oppression of chest ; loose rattling cough, no sputa ; suffocative fits ; face dark purple ; great jactitation of muscles.
Child at birth pale, breathless, gasping, although cord still pulsates. θ Asphyxia neonatorum.
   

VOICE AND LARYNX. TRACHEA AND BRONCHIA. [25] [Ant. t.]
Feeble voice, burning under sternum, cough and sneezing.
He cannot speak a loud word. θ Bronchial croup.
Unable to speak a word. θ Acute œdema of lungs.
Groaning and moaning with a weak, hollow, soundless voice. θ Cholera.
Speech short, interrupted. θ Pneumonia.
Painfulness of larynx to touch ; sawing respiration. θ Croup.
Rattling of mucus when coughing or breathing.
Rattling originates in upper bronchi and can be heard at a great distance. θ Bronchial catarrh.
Great rattling in larynx extending down to trachea, neither cough nor vomiting brought up phlegm.
Tracheal stertor, bronchial rhonci.
Much rattling of mucus in trachea ; cannot get it up.
Bronchiectasis and senile catarrh.
Catarrhal (not membranaceous) croup ; croup of adults.
   

RESPIRATION. [26] [Ant. t.]
Quick breathing.
Breathing quick, short, trembling, as it were. θ Pneumonia.
Breathing frequent. θ Bronchial croup.
Breathing short, frequent. θ Acute catarrh. θ Pertussis.
Children breathe more quickly when lying down than when carried about in an upright position.
Breathing short and difficult. θ Puerperal convulsions.
Shortness of breath from suppressed expectoration, especially if drowsy.
Slow respiration. θ Meningitis.
During sleep, frequent attacks of unequal, intermittent breathing.
The unequal breathing, now shorter, then longer, is much more frequent in lying down, > when child is carried upright. θ Bronchial catarrh.
Breath panting, more depending on abdominal muscles than on chest ; right half of chest immovable. θ Pneumonia.
Gasping inhalation. θ Asthma.
Gasps for air at beginning of every coughing spell.
Gasping. θ Child after birth.
Breathing with a moaning sound, and raising shoulders. θ Catarrhal croup.
Child expels air with a kind of bellowing. θ Pneumonia.
The noise of breathing became more sharp and rough, a continued whistling and purring could be heard in chest. θ Bronchial catarrh.
Sawing respiration. θ Bronchial croup.
Breathing from fifth to seventh rib (r. side behind) indistinct, but bronchial consoning rattling. θ Pneumonia.
Such rattling that is threatens to suffocate child. θ Pneumonia.
Respiration with great rattling of mucus.
Difficulty of breathing, rattling, etc., in convulsions.
Child cannot nurse, but ends each attempt with crying. θ Broncho-pneumonia, etc.
Great difficulty in breathing. θ Convulsions. θ Bronchial catarrh. θ Pneumonia.
Oppression of breathing, relieved by expectoration. θ Influenza.
Every night suffocating attacks. θ Asthma.
If the attack of difficult breathing is very violent at night, all next day breathing is impeded. θ Asthma.
Must be supported in a sitting posture in bed. θ Orthopnea.
Dyspnœa : in croup ; nostrils widely dilated, thorax elevated, much rattling ; with heat in chest ; when awakening.
Not much pain in chest, but much dyspnœa. θ Pneumonia.
Extreme want of breath. θ Pneumonia.
Danger of suffocation with rattling of phlegm, always comes on suddenly. θ Asthma.
Great orthopnea. θ Acute œdema of lungs. θ Dilatation of heart.
Suffocated and oppressed about 3 A. M., must sit up to get air ; after cough and expectoration she became >.
Suffocative attacks with heat about heart.
Spells of suffocation. θ Pneumonia. θ Puerperal convulsions.
Spells of choking, in evening, in bed ; with constriction. θ Pneumonia.
Child is breathless after birth.
Asphyxia : from mechanical causes, as apparent death from drowning ; from pneumonia, capillary bronchitis, atelectasis ; from accumulation of mucus which cannot be expectorated ; neonatorum ; from emphysema, acute œdema pulmonum with hydrothorax ; with impending paralysis of lungs ; accompanied by drowsiness or coma ; pale or dark red face ; blue lips ; delirium, muscular twitchings ; threadlike pulse.
Relieves the "death-rattle."
   

COUGH. [27] [Ant. t.]
Frequent little cough, without expectoration. θ Pneumonia.
Cough day and night, returning at short intervals, no sputa. θ Acute catarrh.
Whooping cough : preceded by the child crying, after eating or drinking, or when getting warm in bed ; after attack, somnolency.
Cough with the peculiar sound of whooping cough.
Cough in attacks, with a hissing hoarseness, raises hand to larynx, which is sensitive to touch. θ Catarrhal croup.
Short cough with a shrill sound. θ Bronchial catarrh.
Tormented from time to time by painful coughs of a shrieking sound. θ Catarrh of a child.
Cough compels patient to sit up, is moist and rattling, but without expectoration. θ Bronchial catarrh.
When child coughs there appears to be a large collection of mucus in bronchial tubes, and it seems as if much would be expectorated, but nothing comes up.
Rattling cough, sounding as if it were moist, without really being so.
Great rattling, but little expectoration. θ Pertussis.
Loose rattling cough, no sputa. θ Puerperal convulsions.
Cough, with dentition of children, in which the râles are so loud that they can be heard at a distance ; disappearing as soon as children finish their bout of coughing.
Between the coughs faint or loud cries for help. θ Catarrhal croup.
Cough, accompanied by crying out ; dizziness ; trembling of head ; drowsiness ; cold sweat on head and hands.
Pale face ; retraction of epigastrium ; retching and vomiting of food.
Violent cough after each meal, ending with vomiting of food. θ Bronchial catarrh.
Cough hollow, excites vomiting, accompanied by great pain. θ Pneumonia.
Tickling cough, with violent eructations and retching, even vomiting of watery, tough slime ; with it a running coryza.
Uninterrupted cough, with frequent vomiting of bloody, frothy, thin fluid masses. θ Acute œdema of lungs.
Cough with suffocating attacks.
Distracting cough day and night, with short breath and rattling in chest. θ Catarrh of a child.
Every cough causes unbearable pains in sides of chest or in abdomen. θ Pneumonia.
Every attempt to cough increases the torture. θ Pneumonia.
Pain in chest when coughing. θ Intermittent.
Cough in variola.
Coughing and gaping consecutively, particularly children ; with crying or dozing, and twitching in face.
Much fatiguing cough, most nights, shaking whole chest and causing headache most in forehead. θ Influenza.
Cough dry, breathing sawing, face red, puffed up, look anxious, could not talk. θ Croup.
Rattling or hollow cough, < at night, with suffocation, throat full of phlegm, sweat on forehead, vomiting food.
Constant irritation to cough, with brown expectoration of sero-albuminous kind. θ Influenza.
Profuse mucus with feeble expulsive power. θ Bronchitis of infants and old people.
Profuse mucous sputa, easily expectorated.
Difficult expectoration, continual shooting pain in left side of chest. θ Pleuritis rheumatica.
Sputa thick and yellow. θ Bronchial catarrh.
Expectoration tough, foamy, mixed with blood. θ Pneumonia.
Frequent cough, with frothy, sanguineous sputa.
Blood spitting when after attack there remains for a long time a bloody, slimy expectoration.
After cough lasts a while, it gets loose and relieves contraction of chest. θ Asthma.
After suffocative fits at night cough with increase of asthma.
Cough grows less frequent, patient shows signs of "carbonized blood."
At 11 P. M. sudden violent cough. θ Acute œdema of lungs.
Cough < every morning. θ Bronchial catarrh.
   

INNER CHEST AND LUNGS. [28] [Ant. t.]
Full feeling of chest.
Crushing weight on chest. θ Variola.
Great oppression on chest. θ Puerperal convulsions.
Oppression before eruption appears. θ Smallpox.
Velvety feeling in chest. θ Heart disease.
Anxious, with oppression of chest and warm rising from heart.
Heat in chest with dyspnœa.
Pain dull, pressing and burning extending to sternum. θ Pneumonia.
Burning in chest extending towards throat.
Violent pains from chest to shoulder, lancinating and tearing. θ Pleuritis rheumatica.
During five hours had at least six pounds of fluid evacuated, and still both lungs seemed filled with a fluid secretion. θ Acute pulmonary œdema.
Motion of chest very quick but heavy, like under a heavy load, with suffocative anxiety and stertorous rattling of phlegm. θ Pneumonia.
Slight motion of chest ; principally abdominal breathing. θ Pneumonia.
Mucous and subcrepitant râles and dull percussion ver summit of right lung.
Rattling of large bubbles with purring in chest. θ With cough.
Constant rattling, can be heard at a distance, mostly on r. side. θ Acute catarrh.
Rattling of phlegm in bronchia very audible, with increased irritation to cough. θ Bronchial catarrh.
Rattling of phlegm on chest, > when carried in an upright position, < lying down ; with oppression. θ Bronchial catarrh. θ Croup.
After pneumonia rattling continuing, with much cough and copious, white, frothy expectoration. θ Pneumonia.
On upper right side and whole left side ; numerous fine râles. θ Pneumonia. θ Œdema of lungs.
Inflammation of respiratory mucous membrane.
Grippe ; acute pneumonia ; broncho-pneumonia ; pleuro-pneumonia.
Sputa blood-streaked, rust-colored, adhering like glue to vessel. θ Pleuro-pneumonia.
Gastric or bilious pneumonia.
Rheumatic affections of pleura or peritoneum. θ Pneumonia.
Strong bronchial breathing in front, right side, above and behind ; crepitation in left lung ; expiratory murmur. θ Pneumonia.
Coarse and fine râles ; very weak vesicular breathing. θ Œdema of lungs.
Complete hepatization. θ Pneumonia.
In front, right side, a dull, empty percussion sound. θ Pneumonia.
Percussion sound tympanitic. θ Œdema of lungs.
Percussion behind and below, right side, up to third rib, empty tympanitic. θ Pneumonia.
Atelectasis, with symptoms of asphyxia belonging to remedy ; with œdema of unhepatized portions of lungs ; breathing labored, orthopnea ; mucous râles. θ Pneumonia.
Œdema of lungs.
Frequent vomiting of a bloody, foamy fluid.
Emphysema.
Impending paralysis of lungs. θ Typhus pneumonia.
   

HEART, PULSE AND CIRCULATION. [29] [Ant. t.]
So warm about heart that she must let arms sink down, with great general weakness. θ Dilatation of heart.
Violent sudden beats of heart. θ Pleurisy.
Palpitation of heart with loose stools.
Pericarditis with pleuro-pneumonia.
Dilatation of heart from rheumatism, with feeling as if heart was strained ; velvety feeling in chest ; warmth about heart ; orthopnea ; cyanosis.
Cyanosis. θ Dilatation of heart.
Pulse frequent. θ Summer complaint.
Pulse increases from 62 to 75 beats, and remains frequent until night. θ Rheumatism.
Pulse frequent, but not quick. θ Bronchial croup.
Pulse frequent and strong.
Pulse very frequent and unequal. θ Catarrh of a child.
Pulse 132, small, hard. θ Pneumonia.
Pulse hard and quick, in old people.
Pulse 112. θ Pneumonia.
Pulse 120 with a child. θ Pneumonia.
Pulse hard, full and strong ; sometimes trembling ; very much accelerated by every motion ; when fever abates it is often slow and imperceptible.
Pulse almost ceases or is violent, reverberating in head. θ Dilatation of heart.
Pulse small and contracted ; t.
Pulse small. θ Influenza.
Pulse quick and small. θ Diarrhœa of a child.
Pulse small, hard, very quick, intermitting. θ Pneumonia.
Pulse weak, quick and trembling. θ Bronchial catarrh.
Threadlike or trembling pulse. θ Cholera.
